With a decentralized structure spanning five strategic locations across the country, Cheshire Ethiopia operates with a team of 210 professionals and non-professional staff, maintaining robust governance, administrative, financial, and procurement processes that meet national and donor requirements. Cheshire Ethiopia, in collaboration with CBM International, is implementing the “Seeing the Future” project a three-year initiative (April 2025 to March 2028) aimed at strengthening inclusive ophthalmic services in underserved regions of Ethiopia. title: Protection Officer - Monitoring
description: Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer - Monitoring for our operations in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered Overall purpose of the role Under the technical supervision of the Protection Manager, the Protection officer (Monitoring), will implement protection monitoring activities in the target locations. Its work focuses on transformative results including ending preventable maternal deaths, unmet need for family planning, and gender-based violence and harmful practices . The Programme Specialist, Gender, GBV and Harmful Practices will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia , within UNFPA Ethiopia's Gender and Social Norms Unit . The role will support a portfolio of programmes addressing gender-based violence (GBV), female genital mutilation (FGM), child marriage, social and gender norm transformation, community engagement, and policy and institutional strengthening . Provide technical and programme support to interventions addressing FGM, child marriage, GBV prevention and response, and social and gender norm transformation . Support national and regional initiatives promoting harmful practices-free communities and sustained social norm change. Strengthen integration of GBV and harmful practices programming with sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), livelihoods and community engagement interventions. Review and provide inputs to concept notes, workplans, Terms of Reference, partner agreements, budgets and programme implementation documents. Coordinate with government institutions, UN agencies, development partners, civil society organizations and implementing partners. Participate in technical working groups, coordination platforms, programme reviews and consultations. Contribute to programme and donor reports, results frameworks, presentations and briefing materials. Document results, lessons learned, good practices, case studies and human-interest stories. Support research, assessments, reviews and evaluations related to GBV, FGM, child marriage and gender/social norm transformation. Develop technical materials, briefs and knowledge products and support strategic communication and advocacy. Contribute to funding proposals, donor briefs, investment cases and resource mobilization initiatives. Profile Required Experience: Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in areas such as: Gender equality Gender-based violence (GBV) Harmful practices Female genital mutilation (FGM) Child marriage Social and gender norm transformation Related development programming Candidates should have experience supporting programme planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting and coordination , as well as knowledge of Ethiopia's policy and institutional environment related to gender equality, GBV and harmful practices. title: MSc in pediatrics and child health nurse specialist
description: Company Description ALERT Hospital is a specialized healthcare institution located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, providing comprehensive services in pediatrics, child health, and related specialties. The hospital is committed to delivering safe, evidence-based, and compassionate care to infants, children, and adolescents. It supports continuous professional development, multidisciplinary collaboration, and quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient outcomes. ALERT Hospital values ethical practice, respect for diverse communities, and a supportive environment for healthcare professionals seeking to advance their careers in pediatric and child health. Role Description The MSc in Pediatrics and Child Health Nurse Specialist will provide advanced nursing care to pediatric patients in inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, and emergency settings. Day-to-day responsibilities include comprehensive assessment, diagnosis support, care planning, medication administration, monitoring patient progress, and coordinating multidisciplinary care with physicians and allied health professionals. The nurse specialist will educate patients, families, and caregivers on disease management, growth and development, nutrition, and preventive health measures, while promoting child-friendly, culturally sensitive care. The role includes participation in clinical protocols, quality and safety initiatives, mentorship of junior staff and students, and documentation in accordance with hospital policies and regulatory standards. This is a full-time, on-site role based at ALERT Hospital in Addis Ababa. Qualifications Master of Science (MSc) in Pediatrics and Child Health Nursing or equivalent advanced degree from a recognized institution. Valid professional nursing license/registration and eligibility to practice in Ethiopia, with documented pediatric clinical experience. Strong skills in pediatric assessment, care planning, medication management, and monitoring of critically and chronically ill children. Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team, demonstrating collaboration, accountability, and respectful communication. Competence in health education for children and families, including counseling on growth, development, immunization, nutrition, and preventive care. Proficiency in maintaining accurate clinical documentation, adherence to infection prevention and patient safety protocols, and use of basic health information systems. Demonstrated ability to supervise, mentor, and support junior nurses and students, and willingness to participate in in-service training and continuing education. Strong problem-solving, time management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to function in high-pressure and resource-limited settings. Commitment to ethical practice, child rights, non-discriminatory care, and respect for diverse cultural, religious, and socioeconomic backgrounds. Basic competency in relevant local languages and good command of English for clinical communication and documentation is an advantage.
